rv.q: The friction between their personalities produces terrific chemistry, and the smart book guarantees that, while their early exchanges are abrasive, they’re also genuinely witty.
That's the entertaining idea behind the sassy new musical comedy, "First Date."
But the show really rests on Levi’s shoulders — and he carries it effortlessly.
But it also displays a genuine wit and musical flair that marks a refreshing change from the onslaught of overblown musicals permeating Broadway these days.
What makes 'First Date' worth seeing is that it knows exactly what it is: a small, sweet, unpretentious musical comedy that aims to please and succeeds.

The songs (by Alan Zachary and ­Michael Weiner, of the upcoming Secondhand Lions) are pleasant, often energetic Broadpop bonbons with better-than-­average lyrics, but apart from Gay Bestie's oft-repeated 'Bailout Song' (performed with flair by Kristoffer Cusick), they won't haunt your dreams or even your cab ride home.
Despite a little overeagerness, First Date isn’t a bad night out (provided you don’t expect deep engagement).
A more appropriate title for 'First Date' would be 'Last Rites.'
Though your head may tell you to cut short this First Date, you find yourself rooting for this unlikely couple (and the show) to succeed.
Austin Winsberg's slapstick book makes hash of every dating cliche we've heard...The breezy if plain score is by young composers Alan Zachary and Michael Weiner, who've written for Disney...
Levi and Rodriguez both sing well, and establish a very winning rapport.

When in the final twenty minutes they offer some straight ballads -- "Safer" for Rodriguez, "In Love with You" for Levi, and the finale "Something That Will Last" -- Zachary and Weiner reveal promise.
'First Date' is harmless and instantly forgettable.
“First Date” — a new Broadway musical about, you guessed it, a first date — is just as generic, pedestrian, bare and altogether uninteresting as the title implies that it will be.
Well, yes — and so is just about everything else in this dopey midsummer entry, which opened Thursday at the Longacre Theatre.
All fine, but not enough to recommend the show.

Staged with wacky buoyancy by director Bill Berry, this is the kind of musical that'll have you remembering the funny moments more than the melodies, but if it's true what they say about a sense of humor being the most attractive quality in a mate, First Date offers up a terrific match.
But Levi and Rodriguez are so refreshingly honest in their interplay, we wind up rooting for them to get together despite the hokey world they inhabit.
